NONE: › the time at which something, especially some type of military activity, is planned to begin
行動開始時間；（尤指軍事行動的）發動時刻
› Indian English in the Indian parliament, the time during which members of parliament can ask questions without arranging to ask them first
› to direct all your attention towards a particular thing

example: We must decide on our target market, then zero in on it.
我們必須確定目標市場，然後將其鎖定。

NONE: › to aim a weapon directly at something or someone

example: Modern military aircraft use computers to help them zero in on their targets.
現代軍用飛機運用電腦來幫助瞄準目標。

NONE: › the act of punishing all criminal or unacceptable behaviour severely, even if it is not very serious
（對犯罪行為無論輕重一律嚴懲的）零容忍政策

example: The police are exercising a new policy of zero tolerance against motoring offenders.
警方現在實施新政策，對駕車肇事者嚴懲不怠。

NONE: › A zero-carbon building, activity, business, etc., is one that does not cause any carbon dioxide to be added to the atmosphere

example: See also

NONE: › an agreement under which an employer can change the number of hours worked by an employee, and does not have to offer any hours
零工時合同（雇主可自由改變雇員工作時間甚至無須保證有任何工作時間的合同）

example: Thousands of workers in the UK are on zero-hours contracts.
在英國，成千上萬的工人簽的是零工時合同。

NONE: › used to refer to a situation in which any win by one person always means a loss to another person involved
一方得益一方受損的；得失所系的

example: The stock market is now a zero-sum game, in which one party gains what the other loses.
股市現在是一種零和遊戲，有人賺就有人虧。
